condition: domestic hoarding of newspapers and mail piled on the floor obstructing hallway and kitchen access over 2 years in an older woman
level_rationale: Two years of saving newspapers and mail and piling them up on the floor in disorganized clutter that blocks the hallway and kitchen in a 67-year-old woman meets functional-impairment criteria for hoarding disorder requiring structured cognitive behavioral therapy for hoarding with a therapist, whereas keeping saved newspapers and mail sorted neatly inside 2 small boxes on a hallway shelf reflects ordinary benign household organization requiring no care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult female lexical register swap (-reg, Subramaniam 2020; Wiktionary) + uncontracted sentimentality causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact household storage organization de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic non-self-harm reference facts (67-year-old woman, 2 years of saving newspapers and mail, and floor clutter blocking hallway and kitchen) with zero apostrophe contractions, a 2-word span difference (20 vs 22 words), and zero stated negatives. Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 inside the same home from floor clutter blocking the hallway and kitchen to 2 neat boxes on a hallway shelf shifts care cleanly from therapist hoarding treatment (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
